title: Trace a data program
instruction: Three short programs work with data. Trace them line by line and watch for where the data and the program part ways.

steps.q: Is the condition t > highest true?
steps.why: -3 is less than 0. The condition is not true and highest stays 0.
No temperature is greater than 0, so the starting 0 stays. The program prints a number that isn’t in the data at all.

steps.q: How do you fix line 2 so that the program works for any numbers?
steps.why: Start with the first real measurement. -1 and -100 only move the bug somewhere else: with data from a laboratory freezer (-150 °C) they would fail again.

code: pupil = find the row in pupils with this id

steps.q: Which pupil does the program find?
steps.why: Id 2 belongs to only one pupil: Ema from 7.A. That is why records are joined through the id, not through the name.
The loans with id 1, 1 and 3 belong to pupils from 7.B. The loan with id 2 belongs to 7.A. The result is 3.

steps.input: a variant: the loans contain the name instead of the id, and the program takes the first pupil with that name
steps.q: What would the program print now?
steps.why: For “Ema” it always finds the first Ema, the one from 7.B. So The Little Prince is counted for the wrong class and the result is 4. A name is not a unique key.

code: draw n pixels in colour colour

steps.q: Which colour is it drawing in now?
steps.why: After the first run, the colour switched from white to black.

steps.input: the loop has finished, 0 = white, 1 = black
steps.q: What does the drawn row look like?

steps.input: you want to encode the row 10000000
steps.q: Which code do you need, if you always start with white?
steps.why: The row starts with black, so the first white run has length 0. Without that zero, the decoder would draw a white pixel and then 7 black ones.

debrief: A program working with data fails where it assumes something that need not be in the data: that temperatures are positive, that a name is unique, that a row starts with white. So test the edges: negative numbers, identical names, empty runs.
